input.content:
THE COMMANDMENTS AND THE LAW OF RESTITUTION

Exodus 20
13 Thou shalt not kill.
14 Thou shalt not commit adultery.
15 Thou shalt not steal.
16 Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
17 Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house: neither shalt thou desire his wife, nor his servant, nor his handmaid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is his.

Exodus 22
1 If any man steal an ox or a sheep, and kill or sell it: he shall restore five oxen for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.
2 If a thief be found breaking open a house or undermining it, and be wounded so as to die: he that slew him shall not be guilty of blood.
3 But if he did this when the sun is risen, he hath committed murder, and he shall die. If he have not wherewith to make restitution for the theft, he shall be sold.
4 If that which he stole be found with him, alive, either ox, or ass, or sheep: he shall restore double.
5 If any man hurt a field or a vineyard, and put in his beast to feed upon that which is other men's: he shall restore the best of whatsoever he hath in his own field, or in his vineyard, according to the estimation of the damage.
6 If a fire breaking out light upon thorns, and catch stacks of corn, or corn standing in the fields, he that kindled the fire shall make good the loss.
7 If a man deliver money, or any vessel unto his friend to keep, and they be stolen away from him that received them: if the thief be found he shall restore double:
8 If the thief be not known, the master of the house shall be brought to the gods, and shall swear that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbour's goods,
9 To do any fraud, either in ox, or in ass, or sheep, or raiment, or any thing that may bring damage: the cause of both parties shall come to the gods: and if they give judgment, he shall restore double to his neighbour.
10 If a man deliver ass, ox, sheep, or any beast, to his neighbour's custody, and it die, or be hurt, or be taken by enemies, and no man saw it:
11 There shall be an oath between them, that he did not put forth his hand to his neighbour's goods: and the owner shall accept of the oath; and he shall not be compelled to make restitution.
25 If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor, that dwelleth with thee, thou shalt not be hard upon them as an extortioner, nor oppress them with usuries.
26 If thou take of thy neighbour a garment in pledge, thou shalt give it him again before sunset.

concepts.folio_definition: The Ten Commandments represents the core moral and religious decalogue that God spoke directly to Israel from Mount Sinai and inscribed on stone tablets, establishing fundamental covenant obligations. These commandments form the essential covenant stipulations governing Israel's relationship with God and neighbor, serving as the foundational ethical framework for biblical law.

Catechists throughout medieval Europe taught the ten commandments as the basic moral framework for examining conscience.
Contemporary legal scholars debated whether displaying the ten commandments in courthouses violated church-state separation principles.

concepts.folio_definition: You Shall Not Kill represents the fifth commandment prohibiting the unlawful taking of human life, establishing life's sacred inviolability as made in God's image. This decree protects human dignity from murder while traditional interpretation permits capital punishment, just war, and legitimate self-defense, distinguishing wrongful killing from authorized life-taking.

Some translators have rendered this commandment as "you shall not murder" to clarify it prohibits wrongful killing rather than all life-taking.
Suicide prevention advocates have extend this commandment to self-killing, emphasizing life belongs to God alone.

concepts.folio_definition: You Shall Not Steal represents the seventh commandment prohibiting the wrongful taking of another's property, protecting rightful ownership and economic justice. This decree establishes respect for legitimate possessions as moral obligation, extending beyond theft to encompass fraud, exploitation, wage theft, and any unjust deprivation of another's goods or labor.
folio_examples: Business ethicists have interpreted this commandment as prohibiting fraudulent accounting, tax evasion, and deceptive business practices.
Catechists have taught this commandment as requiring restitution and repayment when stolen goods could be returned or compensated.
Moral theologians have extended this commandment to intellectual property violations including plagiarism and copyright infringement.
Social justice advocates have applied this commandment to systemic wage theft where employers withheld earned compensation from workers.

concepts.folio_definition: You Shall Not Covet Your Neighbor's Goods represents the tenth commandment's prohibiting envious desire for another's possessions, addressing interior greed and materialism. This decree regulates heart attitudes toward property and wealth, forbidding the disordered longing that breeds discontent, envy, and potential theft while establishing interior detachment and gratitude as moral imperatives.
folio_examples: Confessors have helped penitents recognize how this commandment addressed root desires preceding theft or fraud.
Moral theologians have distinguished between admiring another's possessions and coveting them with resentful envy.
Spiritual directors have applied this commandment to consumerism and comparison culture that bred chronic dissatisfaction.

cache.normalizedText:
THE COMMANDMENTS AND THE LAW OF RESTITUTION

Exodus 20
13 Thou shalt not kill.
14 Thou shalt not commit adultery.
15 Thou shalt not steal.
16 Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
17 Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house: neither shalt thou desire his wife, nor his servant, nor his handmaid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is his.

Exodus 22
1 If any man steal an ox or a sheep, and kill or sell it: he shall restore five oxen for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.
2 If a thief be found breaking open a house or undermining it, and be wounded so as to die: he that slew him shall not be guilty of blood.
3 But if he did this when the sun is risen, he hath committed murder, and he shall die. If he have not wherewith to make restitution for the theft, he shall be sold.
4 If that which he stole be found with him, alive, either ox, or ass, or sheep: he shall restore double.
5 If any man hurt a field or a vineyard, and put in his beast to feed upon that which is other men's: he shall restore the best of whatsoever he hath in his own field, or in his vineyard, according to the estimation of the damage.
6 If a fire breaking out light upon thorns, and catch stacks of corn, or corn standing in the fields, he that kindled the fire shall make good the loss.
7 If a man deliver money, or any vessel unto his friend to keep, and they be stolen away from him that received them: if the thief be found he shall restore double:
8 If the thief be not known, the master of the house shall be brought to the gods, and shall swear that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbour's goods,
9 To do any fraud, either in ox, or in ass, or sheep, or raiment, or any thing that may bring damage: the cause of both parties shall come to the gods: and if they give judgment, he shall restore double to his neighbour.
10 If a man deliver ass, ox, sheep, or any beast, to his neighbour's custody, and it die, or be hurt, or be taken by enemies, and no man saw it:
11 There shall be an oath between them, that he did not put forth his hand to his neighbour's goods: and the owner shall accept of the oath; and he shall not be compelled to make restitution.
25 If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor, that dwelleth with thee, thou shalt not be hard upon them as an extortioner, nor oppress them with usuries.
26 If thou take of thy neighbour a garment in pledge, thou shalt give it him again before sunset.
